extracted.intended_audience: politicians, statesmen, and an educated public interested in political economy, public finance, and the French Revolution
extracted.subtask_description: An argumentative essay-level critique that articulates standards for sound public finance and judges the fiscal conduct of the National Assembly during the French Revolution. Focuses on revenue, taxation, currency, credit, confiscation, and public expenditure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objectives of a financier
rubrics_metrics.description: "The objects of a financier are, then, to secure an ample revenue; to impose it with judgment and equality; to employ it economically; and when necessity obliges him to make use of credit, to secure its foundations in that instance, and forever, by the clearness and candor of his proceedings, the exactness of his calculations, and the solidity of his funds."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is presented as a compact checklist for judging financial stewardship: (1) secure sufficient revenue, (2) impose taxes judiciously and equally, (3) spend economically, and (4) when using credit, ensure transparency, accurate accounting, and solid funding. The essay repeatedly measures the Assembly's conduct against these four requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Taxes proportioned to means and protective of productive capital
rubrics_metrics.description: Taxes should be "equal impositions, proportioned to the means of the citizens, and the least likely to lean heavy on the active capital employed in the generation of that private wealth from whence the public fortune must be derived."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tax policy must protect the productive capital that creates public wealth; unequal distribution and local exemptions that shift burdens to more submissive or orderly districts are condemned. The Assembly's allowing districts to withhold old taxes is given as an example of introducing new, oppressive inequalities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid voluntary 'benevolence' as a substitute for proper taxation
rubrics_metrics.description: The National Assembly's call for a voluntary benevolence ("for a fourth part of the income of all the citizens, to be estimated on the honor of those who were to pay") is criticized as a "rickety offspring of weakness" and as a "tax weak, ineffective, and unequal."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Voluntary contributions mask luxury and selfishness, shift burdens onto productive capital and public-spirited citizens, and are unreliable. Using 'benevolence' in place of systematic, equitable taxation is an anti-pattern that undermines fiscal stability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not rely on patriotic donations or confiscation as sustainable revenue
rubrics_metrics.description: The scheme of patriotic donations and confiscations (taking valuables from churches, crown, citizens) is denounced: it "ruined several trades; they pillaged the crown of its ornaments, the churches of their plate, and the people of their personal decorations." "Never did a state, in any case, enrich itself by the confiscations of the citizens."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confiscation and one-off patriotic gifts are temporary, destructive, and cannot substitute for regular revenue streams. They also carry moral and practical costs (management burdens, compensations, administration debt) that often outweigh any short-term gain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper currency must be optional, convertible, and backed by real deposits
rubrics_metrics.description: Contrast with English practice: "not one shilling of paper money of any description is received but of choice... the whole has had its origin in cash actually deposited... and that it is convertible at pleasure, in an instant, and without the smallest loss, into cash again."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paper money gains commercial value when it is voluntarily accepted, originates in cash deposits, and is freely convertible; asserting legal parity with specie (or forcing acceptance) does not make paper valuable. The Assembly's attempt to treat assignats as equal to metallic money is criticized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Land-bank/assignat security requires full and open valuation and conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Before using confiscated lands as the basis of a circulating currency, one should "first to ascertain the gross value of the estate, the charges of its management and disposition, the incumbrances perpetual and temporary of all kinds that affect it,--then, striking a net surplus, to calculate the just value of the security... then he would indicate the parcels to be sold, and the time and conditions of sale... and the dealer would then know exactly what he purchased."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A land-backed currency must be created like a business mortgage: clear valuation, account of charges and encumbrances, net surplus vested in trustees, explicit sale rules, and open information for potential purchasers/subscribers. Lack of these steps makes the bank a likely bankruptcy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Honour pledges and account fully before issuing paper on confiscated property
rubrics_metrics.description: The Assembly had pledged that estates taken from the Church would be "disengaged of all charges, and employed... to the great and most pressing exigencies of the state", and "that the sum necessary for the year 1791 should be forthwith determined." Burke criticizes issuing sixteen millions sterling of paper before providing rent-rolls, inventories, or estimates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not issue paper money or treat confiscated property as security until you have authenticated estate values, listed charges, and determined the sums needed; issuing credit on unvouched security is a breach of faith and fiscally irresponsible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for all new charges arising from reorganizations and confiscations
rubrics_metrics.description: When confiscated estates are placed under municipal care and used to compensate disbanded offices or to pay pensions/interest, the Assembly "threw upon this fund... a new charge" which must be ascertained; the report showed ecclesiastical confiscation left a net annual shortfall and debt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before treating confiscated assets as surplus, governments must enumerate and compare all attendant expenses (management costs, pensions, maintenance, municipal charges) against revenues; hidden or unaccounted charges can defeat the purpose of confiscation as a resource.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduce prodigal public expenditure, including one's own institutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Economy should include cutting wasteful expenses: "lessening of prodigal expenses, and the economy which has been introduced... Have those who say so looked at the expenses of the National Assembly itself? of the municipalities? of the city of Paris? of the increased pay of the two armies? of the new police? of the new judicatures? ... the present will be found beyond all comparison more chargeable."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fiscal prudence requires examining and trimming all branches of public expenditure (legislative bodies, municipalities, armies, police, courts, pensions). Claiming economy while expanding new costly institutions is hypocritical and destructive of public finance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain creditworthiness by avoiding coercion and preserving trust
rubrics_metrics.description: Foreign creditors will not advance to a people "who attempt to reverse the very nature of things,--amongst whom they see the debtor prescribing at the point of the bayonet the medium of his solvency to the creditor..." The ancient government's credit allowed borrowing on terms; revolutionary coercion destroys that confidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sovereign credit depends on trust: policies that coerce creditors, alter contractual expectations, or show arbitrary treatment of obligations will cut off access to foreign and domestic capital. Liberty alone does not guarantee credit; credible, stable institutions do.

rubrics_metrics.name: Printing more depreciated paper to cover losses is a self-defeating practice
rubrics_metrics.description: When assignats depreciate the response "Issue new assignats" is ridiculed: "Are the old assignats depreciated at market? What is the remedy? Issue new assignats." This iterative emission further depreciates currency and undermines real money.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resorting to repeated emissions of paper to mask depreciation or pay obligations aggravates inflation, encourages market arbitrage (collectors receiving coin and accounting in depreciated paper), and harms public finances. It is compared to historic financial follies (e.g., Law's schemes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate public measures by net relief to the people, not appearances of relief
rubrics_metrics.description: Burke asks whether people are truly relieved by the destruction of revenue and argues we must solve: whether it is more advantageous "to pay considerably and to gain in proportion, or to gain little or nothing and to be disburdened of all contribution?" He favors paying and gaining proportionally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy should be assessed on real net benefits to the population. Measures that 'relieve' people by destroying productive revenue or by shifting burdens deceptively are cruel impostures. The correct test is whether a measure increases real welfare in proportion to its cost, not whether it reduces nominal contributions.
